ordinary.text: Reuse items that are clean, intact, still usable, and designed to be used again.
steps: Check the item's condition and function before using it again.
Use it the way the material or manufacturer instructions say, and only for safe purposes.

ordinary.text: Recycle the item through a collector that confirms they accept this type and condition.
steps: Confirm the material with the collector, and that they accept this type of item in this condition.
Separate any parts they ask for and follow the collector's preparation instructions.
Hand it over through the route you confirmed, including a specialist collector where needed.

ordinary.text: Choose Trash for non-hazardous residual waste once the item is no longer usable and no recycling route accepts it.
steps: Make sure the item has no batteries, chemicals, or biological contamination.
Separate any parts a collector can still accept.
Use your official local residual waste collection.

ordinary.text: Choose Trash for non-hazardous residual waste when you aren't reusing the item and no recycler accepts it.
steps: Look for ways to reuse it or give it to someone who needs it.
Make sure the item has no batteries, chemicals, or biological contamination.
Use your official local residual waste collection.

organic.text: Recycling organic waste means taking it to a composting program that accepts this kind of scrap.
steps: Separate organic scraps from plastic, stickers, and packaging.
Confirm the program accepts this kind of food or plant waste. Meat, oil, and processed food need a program that takes them.
Follow the composting program's collection instructions.

organic.text: Choose Trash for non-hazardous organic scraps when no composting or organic collection is available to take them.
steps: Separate packaging and other items from the organic scraps.
Use your official residual waste collection under local rules.

electronic.text: Reuse working electronics, or pass them on, following their purpose and the manufacturer's instructions.
steps: Check for damage, overheating, or a swollen battery before using it again.
Wipe your personal data before giving the device to someone else.

electronic.text: Take the electronics to a specialist collection program that confirms they accept the device in its condition.
steps: Contact the electronics collector to confirm they accept this device type and condition.
Protect your personal data before handing it over, if you can do so safely.
Follow their packaging instructions, and don't put it in the trash or mixed recycling.
